# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The incumbent is already timing-feasible at 10 ns (routed WNS 0.272 ns, WHS 0.118 ns) and uses 15 LUTs and 19 FFs; the objective is strictly fewer LUTs, or equal LUTs with fewer FFs. The core’s two-bit `count` and occupancy `case` control the two data registers, while the top is only a wrapper. The top requires `// @latency 1`; preserve its registered output and minimum one-cycle transfer age.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the occupancy count and its case decode with two entry-valid bits and direct push/pop transitions may reduce LUT use, and may also reduce the state FF count, while preserving the FIFO’s full, empty, stall, and simultaneous-transfer behavior.

## Instruction for generator
In `skid_buffer_core`, replace `reg [1:0] count` and the `case (count)` occupancy control with head-valid and tail-valid state; derive `out_valid` from head-valid and `in_ready` from tail-valid and `out_ready`. Keep the two 8-bit storage registers, and rewrite their updates so push into empty loads the head, push into a one-entry queue loads the tail, and a pop from full advances the tail into the head, with simultaneous full pop/push loading the new input into the tail. Preserve synchronous active-high reset priority, pre-edge handshakes, stall stability, throughput, and the top’s `// @latency 1`; retain the candidate only if all verification and routed metric gates pass and the LUT objective improves.
